correctness.rationale: The affine reparameterization was reconstructed from the codimension-one Jacobian \(|\det A|/\|A^Tu\|\), the support-function width factor \(\|A^Tu\|\), and volume scaling. For the cube, the rectangular-section chamber gives \(F=(a+b+c)/a\in[1,2]\). In the hexagonal chamber, the corner-triangle area calculation gives the displayed rational expression. With \(a=y+z\), \(b=z+x\), \(c=x+y\), the exact identities reduce the lower separation from 2 to \(8xyz>0\) and the upper bound to the AM-GM inequality \((x+y+z)(xy+xz+yz)\ge9xyz\). Equality gives the claimed coordinate-axis minimum and body-diagonal maximum. Independent geometric section reconstruction and random affine tests agreed with the analytic profile; the proof itself is all-direction analytic.

evidence: The minimax papers establish broad inequalities and ellipsoid characterizations but do not evaluate the parallelotope directional profile.
König--Koldobsky optimize a different functional, section perimeter, and cite classical cube section-volume extrema rather than the area-times-width product.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader general inequalities and separate section extrema do not determine the same direction-dependent product because width changes with direction and the product maximum need not coincide with either factor's separate maximum.

originality.rationale: The primary 2025 minimax paper formulates the normalized central-section/width functional as Busemann--Petty Problem 6 and proves general minimax inequalities, but its accessible full text does not discuss cubes or parallelotopes or state the directional range \([1,9/4]\). The related inscribed-cone and cube-section literature treats general minimax dualities or section perimeter/volume extrema, not the normalized product profile. No inspected theorem implies both extrema and equality directions for the full affine parallelotope class.
residual_risks: Classical cube-slicing literature contains many exact central-section formulas; an older differently phrased computation of this particular area-times-width profile could exist even though no covering source was found.

The 2023 related inscribed-cone paper was available in this run through its detailed abstract/bibliographic page rather than complete article text; it did not present a decisive same-object claim in the accessible material.

The result is not a tiny arbitrary slice: affine covariance turns one cube calculation into the full parallelotope class.
residual_risks: The exact 9/4 value is only three-dimensional; higher-dimensional cube profiles require separate analysis.
